text:
Sergio Costa: heads up: proposing alert tuning for hot-route throttling spikes before we start the planned load tests next week. current draft is noisy in staging and will definitely page during perf-canary bursts.

Sergio Costa: TL;DR: page only when enterprise lane is impacted OR throttling correlates w/ saturation; otherwise ticket. details below.

Aisha Bello: +1. the existing alert is basically `throttled_count > 0` at route granularity lol. we need thresholds + better grouping.

Sean Gallagher: what are you thinking for paging thresholds? we need something simple enough for oncall at 3am.

Sergio Costa: proposal v1:
1) PAGE (P1): enterprise lane throttling ratio sustained > 1% for 5m AND request volume > 50 rps (to avoid low traffic noise)
   metric: `gateway_throttled_requests / gateway_total_requests` filtered `tier=enterprise` AND `reason in (lane_over_capacity, router_backpressure)`
2) PAGE (P2): burn rate style: enterprise hot routes p99 latency SLO burn > 10x for 5m with `throttled_ratio > 0.5%`
3) TICKET: self-serve throttling ratio > 10% for 10m OR sudden change > +5% absolute in 2m (for regression detection)

Sergio Costa: also: if we’re in an announced load test window, suppress P1/P2, keep ticket + dashboard annotation.

Rafael Mendes: re suppress: please don’t fully silence. we still want signal if something goes sideways. maybe inhibit only if `load_test=true` label is present?

Connor O'Brien: for the perf-canary jobs we can set a header so the gateway emits `traffic_class=synthetic` or something. not sure it’s plumbed everywhere yet.

Benji Okafor: feature flag side: we can add an annotation when `hot_route_protection_enabled` flips, but the alerts don’t have that context unless we add it to the metrics.

Allison Grant: careful with labels. we can’t add `tenant_id` or raw route paths in alerting queries. if we do route, it needs to be `route_id` from the canonical set. also cap cardinality on `reason` (keep it to like 6 values).

Amara Diallo: gateway currently emits `throttle_reason` as a string enum (about ~8 values). route label is `route_template` today, which may still be high-card if folks have funky templates. we can switch to `route_id` once policy engine config lands.

Mina Haddad: router side: we can expose `lane=enterprise|default` + `admit=false` counts. i’d rather the page be on `lane=enterprise` admission drops than on 429s alone, since 429s may be gateway quota not capacity.

Logan Wright: +1. we should distinguish quota enforcement vs overload shedding. those have different oncall actions.

Sergio Costa: good point. updated conditions:
- PAGE only if `reason in (lane_over_capacity, router_backpressure, runtime_saturation)`
- TICKET if `reason=quota_exceeded` spikes (points to billing/metering or customer behavior)

Aisha Bello: can we add a “false positive guard” for deploys? like if the spike coincides w/ `deploy_in_progress` then downgrade? we’ve been burned before.

Rafael Mendes: i’m not a fan of auto-downgrade. but we can add a runbook note: check #eng-releases and recent deploys. also add alert annotations for deploys.

Incident Bot: (auto) Recent deploy detected in us-east-1: router v2025.01.19.3 started at 10:11 UTC. Link: https://deploy.redwood.example/releases/router/2025.01.19.3

Sean Gallagher: can we define “sustained” precisely? 5m is fine but we should use 2/3 evaluation windows to avoid flapping.

Sergio Costa: yep: 3 evaluation points, require 2/3 firing. also add a 20m re-notify interval for P1 so we don’t spam.

Allison Grant: also please don’t group-by `route_id` in the pager. group-by `region` + include top 3 routes in the alert description (via dashboard link). paging per-route will explode during incidents.

Sergio Costa: agreed. pager grouping = `{region, lane}` only. body includes Grafana link with template variables and a “top routes by throttled_ratio” panel.

Amara Diallo: re load tests: today we can’t reliably label synthetic in prod traffic. but Connor’s header idea is doable. until then, can we schedule a silence only for the perf-canary channel window and keep enterprise lane pages enabled?

Connor O'Brien: planned test schedule is 30 min windows, region-by-region. i can post in #eng-oncall before each one and create an alertmanager silence scoped to `source=perf-canary` once the label exists. short term: manual silence scoped to `cluster=canary` only.

Rafael Mendes: +1 manual silence for canary clusters, NOT for prod. also let’s add a checklist item: “if load test ongoing, expect elevated self-serve throttling; enterprise lane should stay <1%”.

Aisha Bello: what about thresholds per region? us-west is smaller, will hit higher ratios with same absolute throttles.

Sergio Costa: i’d rather keep one global rule but require min volume. if `total_requests < 10 rps` we don’t page. that should avoid the tiny-region noise.

Mina Haddad: for router admission drops: we should include absolute count too. 1% of 20 rps = nothing, but could still be important if it’s a top enterprise route. maybe a second clause: `enterprise_admission_drops > 100/min`.

Sean Gallagher: ok. make it: PAGE if (ratio > 1% AND rps > 50) OR (drops > 100/min). keep it simple.

Sergio Costa: works. i’ll update alert definitions + send for review. dashboard panel updates are in observability-pack PR, will add these as well.

Allison Grant: please add “reason code mapping” to the runbook so oncall knows what `runtime_saturation` vs `router_backpressure` implies.

Sergio Costa: will do. linking draft runbook section here (WIP): https://redwood-inference.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRE/pages/214508/Overload+Throttling+Response#Alert-reason-codes

Rafael Mendes: cool. once it’s merged, can we run a mini game-day where we intentionally trigger self-serve throttling and confirm no paging? that’s the main risk.

Sean Gallagher: +1. schedule it after the alert change lands but before we enable the enterprise lane widely.

Sergio Costa: action items:
- Sergio: update alert rules (grouping, thresholds, reasons) + PR today
- Connor: confirm canary cluster labels + silence plan for perf tests
- Amara/Mina: confirm reason enums + which metrics exist gateway vs router
- Allison/Aisha: quick cardinality + SLO burn-rate sanity check

Aisha Bello: :thumbsup: ping me when the PR is up.

Benji Okafor: also FYI: when hot-route protection flag is toggled, i can emit an `event` metric for alert annotations. will follow up in #eng-platform.

Sean Gallagher: thanks all. goal is: real pages == enterprise pain or fleet saturation. everything else should be visible but not wake people up.
